title: Prime Minister pays homage to brave participants of the Quit India Movement
body_text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has remembered all those who participated in the historic Quit India Movement and paid tribute to their courage and determination in India’s freedom struggle. Shri Modi said that inspired by the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, the clarion call of the Quit India Movement infused new energy into the freedom struggle and reflected the unwavering resolve of the people of India to break free from colonial rule.
The Prime Minister posted on X:
Remembering all those who participated in the historic Quit India Movement. Their courage will always remain an inspiration for every Indian. Inspired by the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi Ji, the clarion call of Quit India infused new energy into our freedom struggle and reflected the unwavering determination of our people to break free from colonial rule.

enrichment.summary: On 9 August 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute via a post on X to all participants of the Quit India Movement, commemorating its anniversary. He stated that the movement, inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's leadership, infused new energy into India's freedom struggle and reflected the unwavering resolve of Indians to end colonial rule.
enrichment.context: The Quit India Movement (also known as the August Kranti or 'Bharat Chhodo Andolan') was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 at the All India Congress Committee session in Bombay, with the famous 'Do or Die' call, demanding an immediate end to British rule in India. It came in the backdrop of the failure of the Cripps Mission and growing frustration with Britain's refusal to grant self-government even as India was drawn into World War II. The movement saw mass civil disobedience, underground resistance, parallel governments (such as in Satara and Ballia), and large-scale participation of students, workers, and peasants, met with severe British repression including the arrest of top Congress leadership. Though it did not immediately achieve independence, it demonstrated the depth of popular nationalist sentiment and hastened the process leading to eventual independence in 1947. 9 August is observed annually as 'August Kranti Din' to commemorate the movement, and such commemorative statements by the Prime Minister are a recurring feature of the government's engagement with the legacy of the freedom struggle, part of a broader pattern of using historical anniversaries to reinforce national memory and civic pride.

prelims_questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in response to the failure of which mission/proposal?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement of August 1942 was launched after the failure of the Cripps Mission (March 1942), which failed to satisfy Indian demands for immediate self-government.

prelims_questions.question: On which date was the Quit India Resolution passed by the All India Congress Committee, giving rise to Gandhi's 'Do or Die' call?
prelims_questions.explanation: The AICC passed the Quit India Resolution on 8 August 1942 in Bombay, after which Gandhi gave his famous 'Do or Die' call; the movement's anniversary is commemorated as August Kranti Din on 9 August.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Quit India Movement in the trajectory of India's freedom struggle and assess its impact on British colonial policy.
"The Quit India Movement was less about immediate success and more about demonstrating the depth of mass nationalist sentiment." Critically examine this statement.
